newsitem.title: USA: Profit-taking takes techs, Nasdaq COMPOSITE LOWER.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking takes techs, Nasdaq COMPOSITE LOWER.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite closed lower on Tuesday as profit-taking depressed high technology stocks after an early rally.
Semiconductors initially posted healthy gains, leading techs and the Nasdaq higher after the November book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.15 from an upwardly revised 1.11 in October.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 3.71 points, or 0.28 percent, at 1312.56 at its unofficial close while gainers led losers by 2232 to 2147 on volume of about 681 million shares.
Microsoft Corp was up 1/8 at 81-7/8 after climbing as high as 84-9/16. Intel Corp fell one to 129-1/8. Dell Computer Corp was down 7/8 at 59-5/8.

"The book-to-bill was an unmistakable sell signal," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "If you are a trader you have to seize the day and sell. You won't see news this good for a while."

High techs which took a pounding today included Cascade Communications Corp, down 6-5/8 at 61-7/8, Komag Inc, down 5-7/8 at at 27-1/4, Informix Corp, down 1-1/2 at 24-3/8 and Gateway 2000 Inc, down 5-1/4 at 58-7/8. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index was down 1.99 percent, dropping 5.02 points to 247.26.
